children.translated_text: Now, therefore, we shall explain the Pāśupata yoga-procedure of <s>Paśupati</s>.
One should bathe three times a day with ash.
One should lie down in ash.
There is rinsing after bathing.
There is the offering of the deity's remnants.
One should wear the liṅga (emblem).
One should dwell in the sanctuary.
One should attend upon him with laughter, song, dance, the sound duṃduṃ, prostration, muttered prayer, and offering.
This is for <s>Mahādeva</s> facing south.
One may wear a single garment.
Or one may wear no garment.
One should not look at urine or feces.
One should not converse with a woman or a Śūdra.
If one should look, or if one should converse,
having sipped water for purification,
and having performed breath-control,
one should recite the <s>Raudrī Gāyatrī</s> or the <s>Bahurūpī</s>.
This applies to one whose mind is unstained,
while he is practicing.
Then his yoga begins to operate.
For him seeing, hearing, reflection, and knowledge also begin to operate.
There is omniscience,
the speed of the mind,
the ability to assume any desired form,
freedom from bodily instruments,
and possession of dharma.
And all beings become subject to his control.
And he becomes subject to none of them.
And he enters into all beings.
And he cannot be entered by any of them.
And all beings become capable of being slain by him.
And he becomes incapable of being slain by any of them.
He is fearless,
imperishable,
unaging,
immortal,
and everywhere his movement is unobstructed.

children.text: ity etair guṇair yukto bhagavato mahādevasya mahāgaṇapatir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with these qualities, he becomes the great lord of hosts of the blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Here one should recite this brahman.
I take refuge in <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
In birth after birth, do not carry me beyond becoming.
Favor me.
O source of becoming.
<s>Vāma</s>,
of the god,
of the eldest,
of <s>Rudra</s>,
whose seat has been arranged.
They call it one that grants all desires.
Here the inauspicious becomes auspicious.
And the counterclockwise becomes circumambulation to the right.
Therefore he is to be worshipped in both ways,
as a god and as an ancestor.
For in <s>Rudra</s> both are present: gods and ancestors.
One should be joyful and not negligent.
In each and every observance,
one obtains greatness.
What has been given exceedingly, what has been sacrificed exceedingly,
and austerity practiced with extreme heat,
he brings to a surpassing goal.
Therefore,
one should practice austerity still more.
But there should be devotion to no other than <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Here one should recite this brahman.

children.text: vāmadevāya namo jyeṣṭhāya namo rudrāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>, homage to the eldest, homage to <s>Rudra</s>.
Homage to <s>Kāla</s>.
Homage to the transformer of time.
Homage to the crusher of strength.
Homage to the subduer of all beings.
Homage to him whose mind is beyond mind.
Having an unmanifest sign, but manifest conduct,
despised
among all beings,
he should practice while being insulted.
His evil is removed through the censure of others.
And he gives sin to them.
And he takes their merit.
Therefore,
he should behave like a dead man.
Or he should snore.
Or he should twitch.
Or he should limp.
Or he should act amorously.
He should do even what is improper.
He should say even what is improper.
By that he should incur contempt.
For the learned man, when he is despised, becomes one whose austerity is complete.
Here one should recite this brahman.
To the non-terrible forms,
and then to the terrible forms,
and to those more terrible than the terrible,
to all,
to every form of <s>Śarva</s>,
homage be to you, the forms of <s>Rudra</s>.
The hidden knowledge is revealed for endless austerity.
With a hidden vow and hidden purifying speech,
closing all the doors
with the intellect,
one should wander alone in the world like a madman.
One should take prepared food that has been discarded.

children.text: unmatto mūḍha ityevaṃ manyante itare janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Other people think, 'He is mad, he is confused,' in just this way.
For disrespect is remembered as the highest of all instruments.
In ancient times <s>Indra</s> practiced the Pāśupata observance among the Asuras.
He took away their sacrifice and charitable works.
Through well-made illusion he obtained them.
For their blame is really no blame; therefore,
one should practice while being blamed.
His conduct should be blameless.
This path is distinguished above all.
It is the true path.
Other paths are bad paths.
Having gone near <s>Rudra</s> by this procedure,
no Brāhmaṇa returns again.
Here one should recite this brahman.
May we know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
May we meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s>.
May that <s>Rudra</s> impel us.
Unattached,
a yogin,
with the self eternal,
unborn,
friendly,
he is born through conquest of the senses; <s>Rudra</s> spoke thus far.
He should dwell in an empty house or a cave.
He should be devoted constantly to the god, with conquered senses.
For one constantly disciplined, after six months
the greater result begins to arise.

children.text: bhaikṣyam pātrāgatam māṃsam aduṣyaṃ lavaṇena vā ||
children.translated_text: Alms that have come into the bowl, meat that is not impure, or food with salt,
or even water, he should eat at the proper time and in due order.
Following the way of cattle or the way of deer,
he should become pure by water alone.

children.text: siddhayogī na lipyate karmaṇā pātakena vā ||
children.translated_text: A perfected yogin is not stained by action or by sin.
Self-controlled, he should recite the chosen ṛc or the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Or the <s>Raudrī</s>, or the <s>Bahurūpī</s>.
From this, yoga begins to operate.
One should meditate on the syllable oṃ.
One should establish concentration in the heart.
This is the seer, the Brāhmaṇa, the great one,
pure in speech,
<s>Maheśvara</s>.
Dwelling in a cremation ground,
righteous in self, living on whatever is obtained, he gains union with <s>Rudra</s>.
He should always remember <s>Rudra</s>.
Having cut the root of the network of causes of faults,
with the intellect,
the composed mind,
and having fixed it on <s>Rudra</s>,
alone, secure, and free from sorrow.
Being vigilant, he should proceed to the end of sufferings through the grace of <s>Īśa</s>.
Here he should recite this Brahman formula:
"<s>Īśāna</s> is lord of all branches of knowledge;
<s>Īśvara</s> is lord of all beings;
the lord of Brahman, <s>Brahmā</s>, may <s>Śiva</s> be favorable to me;
always <s>Śiva</s>."
